positive: Many commenters praise the opening and closing animation as smooth, clean and seamless, with some saying the design team deserves recognition.
Several viewers, including self-described Apple skeptics and Samsung fans, admit the blur or see-through fold effect is clever and distinctly Apple.
Commenters say the crease is barely visible or absent, and credit the matte inner screen finish with helping to hide it.
negative: Many commenters say the crease is still clearly visible despite Apple's claims, with some noting it shows up in certain lighting.
Several worry the crease will worsen with repeated folding, and think the matte screen only hides it while dulling colors.
The fold animation draws skepticism: some see it as hype over a minor feature, and it looks glitchy or odd on the inner screen.

positive: Several Samsung foldable owners say they are impressed by Apple's first foldable and admit it looks good.
Others like the thoughtful software choices, such as moving the menu bar to where the thumb rests, while some say they will stay with Samsung.
negative: Many commenters say Samsung and other Android makers released foldables years earlier, so Apple's entry looks late and is not an innovation.
Commenters mock Apple fans and marketing for treating a long-existing feature as groundbreaking, and note Apple once dismissed the idea.
Some criticise Apple's foldable on its drawbacks: high price, visible crease, laggy animations and missing specs, while noting Samsung's cheaper deals.

positive: Many commenters were pleasantly surprised by the Duo's look, praising its minimal crease, matte inner screen and polished unfolding animation despite expecting to dislike it.
Several Samsung Fold users say the Fold 8 looks better, citing its thinness, light weight and design, while others welcome Apple to foldables.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is arriving years after Samsung and Google, and mock fans and marketing for presenting foldables as new.
Several dislike the Duo's design: the asymmetric, rounded outer shape and front screen look odd, and it seems small, bulky and dated next to the Samsung.
Price is a frequent complaint, with commenters saying Samsung's Fold costs much less, in some countries about half, while being thinner and lighter.

positive: Many commenters expected a much higher price and were pleasantly surprised the foldable launched at around the two-thousand-dollar mark.
Pricing in line with Samsung's foldables is seen as competitive and normal for the category, even good value once inflation is considered.
negative: Many commenters see the foldable's price as excessive and unjustified, and some joke that the name reflects paying for two phones.
Regional pricing draws criticism: people in India, Turkey, Australia and elsewhere say local prices are much higher and out of reach.
Some say the cost isn't worth it for them, since their current phone works fine or they want less screen time.

positive: Many commenters prefer a clean, uninterrupted inner screen over a visible cutout or dot, saying hidden selfie cameras suit media viewing and reading.
Several say selfie quality matters little to them, since they rarely take photos or would use the outer display's camera for selfies anyway.
Some praise the camera's disappearing effect and screen animations as polished, and expect other makers to push under-display technology forward.
negative: Under-display cameras are seen as old technology that other brands tried and dropped because image quality was poor.
The camera is still visible through the screen, so it doesn't fully disappear, and the 'feature' is seen as lowering quality expectations.
Some commenters would still prefer an under-display camera over a punch-hole on the inner screen, and others say selfies don't matter to them.

positive: Many left-handed commenters say they have always adapted to right-handed designs, so the Duo's layout is not a dealbreaker for them.
Several lefties say they already hold their phone in the right hand or use both hands, so it makes little difference.
Some expect software options, such as mirroring the interface to the left side, and think the concern is overblown.
negative: Many commenters say the Duo's hardware layout favors right-handed use, with fixed Touch ID, outer display and cameras, so software fixes alone wouldn't help lefties.
Some left-handed users say they would skip the device or wait for a later version, rather than hold it awkwardly or upside down.
Others raise wider one-handed usability worries, including people with limited use of one arm and those who prefer holding the phone in their non-dominant hand.

positive: Several commenters welcome Apple Pencil support on the foldable, noting that rival foldables lack pen support, which makes the Apple device more appealing.
Pencil support, together with the larger inner screen, makes viewers picture the device as a mini iPad for productivity and note-taking.
Commenters mention that only the USB-C Pencil works, which means it has to be plugged in to charge or pair.
negative: Many commenters see Apple's pencil support as a late imitation of Samsung rather than real innovation, and mock Apple fans for celebrating it.
Some worry a first-generation foldable screen may be fragile, with pen use risking scratches or damage and repair costs falling on owners.
Several Samsung fans say Samsung's own missing S-Pen support on recent folds is the real disappointment, and want it brought back.

positive: The matte nano-texture inner display is liked for cutting glare and reflections, and some think it helps hide the fold crease and adds privacy.
Overall reaction is enthusiastic, with some saying the Duo looks better than rival foldables and wanting one, though one commenter disputes calling nano-texture matte.
negative: Several commenters see "nano-texture" as just a fancy marketing name for a matte screen, not a real innovation.
Some say the matte finish makes the unfolded inner display look grainy, which hurts the viewing experience.
Commenters worry about the inner screen's durability, such as scratches, and doubt that multitasking with several apps really improves productivity.

positive: Many commenters are openly excited and plan to pre-order or buy the Duo as soon as possible, with some counting down to launch.
Several long-time iPhone owners say the Duo is the reason to finally upgrade, and some will trade in or sell current phones.
negative: Price is the main barrier: many call it too expensive and say they will keep their current phone or choose a Pro Max.
Many plan to wait for a later generation, expecting a lighter, more refined, more durable version after first-generation flaws.
Concerns about weight, hinge and screen durability, app scaling, and downgrades from Pro features such as cameras; some say an iPad mini suffices.

positive: Viewers like how the official cases look in use, saying a plain design appears sleek and appealing once fitted to the phone.
Some note the Apple case includes a built-in stand, which makes using the device in a sideways orientation easy.
Many commenters say the case and presentation make them more excited and more likely to buy the Duo, despite missing buttons or high cost.
negative: Many commenters say the price is too high, especially for larger storage tiers, and that a case and AppleCare add even more.
Some note the phone is heavy and wobbles on a surface, and expect a case to help only partly or add bulk.
Others feel the visible crease and missing features make it a poor buy, and suggest cheaper alternatives such as a tablet.

positive: Many like that the folded phone is small and pocketable, with some saying it fills the gap left by the iPhone mini while still offering a big unfolded screen.
Software and screen handling get praise, including smooth transitions between screens, a space-saving side toolbar, easy back gestures and an attractive outer display.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable form factor isn't new, pointing to existing foldables and the Surface Duo, and describe Apple as copying others.
Some worry about durability and missing features, such as foldable screens failing after about a year and no Face ID at a very high price.
Others doubt app support, expecting developers not to optimise for the new form factor, so apps will run poorly at launch.

positive: Many commenters praise how smoothly Apple's hardware and software work together, calling the software polished and top quality.
Apple's software experience is seen as the main differentiator, and existing ecosystem ties make some viewers likely to stay with it.
Some are hopeful the device will push third-party developers to optimise apps for foldables, while a few still prefer Samsung's software flexibility.
negative: Many commenters say Apple's software features and foldable concept are not new, pointing to existing foldable phones and to iPadOS multitasking as earlier examples.
Some feel Apple is getting too much credit for ideas that competitors and its own iPad software already offered.
A few have practical doubts: the cover screen's shape looks awkward when closed, and they question how durable the hinge is and whether the warranty covers repeated opening.

positive: Many commenters express strong enthusiasm for the iPhone Duo, with some planning to buy it immediately, and a few Android users admitting admiration or switching.
Frequent comparisons with Samsung's Fold favour the Duo for looks, build quality, performance, iOS and value, though some note the Fold is lighter and thinner.
Several comments mention the Duo's weight, with some accepting it as a result of premium materials, while others hope for slim bezels on future products.
negative: Many commenters mock the name and design, calling the foldable awkward-looking, a missed chance at a better name, and an unsatisfying shape for people who like symmetry.
Weight and thickness come up often: the phone is described as the heaviest iPhone yet, hard to use one-handed, and underreported by reviewers.
Price is a major complaint, especially for the base storage tier, with regional prices cited as extreme and compared unfavorably to cheaper models with more features.

positive: Some commenters push back on durability worries, noting the tested unit was only a plastic dummy and the real phone uses titanium.
Several defend the high price, saying it reflects the two-screen folding design and that other folding phones cost about as much.
Many are excited about the fold animation, iOS ecosystem integration and tablet-plus-phone convenience, with some saying Apple finally made folding phones appealing.
negative: Many worry the folding screen and its crease will wear out quickly, and that one drop could ruin the phone, especially with few good protective cases.
Commenters say the device is heavy and bulky, closer to a small tablet than a phone.
Price is the dominant complaint: about double a normal flagship, with entry storage seen as too small for the cost.

positive: Viewers praise the review and the design, including the opening animation, the software look on the foldable screen, and the vertical use.
Many see practical uses for a larger pocketable screen, such as reading documents, medical charts, school work, or passing time during treatment.
Some commenters plan to buy it because of Apple ecosystem loyalty, while others stay with or recommend rival foldables from Samsung, Google or OnePlus.
negative: Commenters praise the videos but say they won't buy the Duo, mainly because first-generation products and the high price put them off.
Several see hardware compromises as dealbreakers: weaker cameras than Pro models, no Face ID, missing features, and rounded corners that cut into usable screen.
Some worry about the hinge's durability, or prefer other foldables or regular phones, or plan to wait for Apple's next release.

positive: Many commenters see the foldable as a way to replace or carry less of an iPad, combining phone and tablet in one pocketable device.
The larger inner screen is praised for video, reading, viewing plans and photos, and for making bigger text easier on tired eyes.
negative: Many see the inner display as little more than a small tablet-style screen, with a matte finish that looks dull and washed out in bright light.
The roughly $2,000 price is widely seen as unjustified for a slightly bigger screen, a small outer display, and reused parts.

positive: Commenters like iOS being adapted for a foldable, citing multitasking, layout tweaks like a movable dock for left-handers, and apps fitting without extra optimization.
Some Android users say they would switch, or only want a foldable because it runs iOS, which they find simple, even if rivals have strong hardware.
Reactions are mostly excited, with praise for the design and expected business appeal. A few find the high price less bad than expected.
negative: Many commenters say the foldable price is too high, especially outside the US, where conversion and taxes push it far above the US price.
Android users say Samsung and others have offered foldables for years, so Apple's version feels late and gives them no reason to switch.
Some criticize Apple's presentation as evasive or overhyped, and dislike the design, the camera, and the multitasking compared with Android.

positive: The one-sided rounded corners get a warm response, described as notebook-like, softer in the pocket and easier to hold, with a balanced look when open.
Some viewers like the glass-style opening animation and Liquid Glass interface, and a few mention the hinge or build feeling durable.
negative: Commenters say the hinge isn't new, likening it to existing foldables from rivals and finding the reviewer's amazement overblown.
Skeptical about water resistance: they note a competing foldable with a high rating still failed, and that it has other weak fold points.
Some feel the design borrows from others while cutting corners, and that the price is too high for the storage.

positive: Many viewers are eager for the device and plan to wait and buy it once it launches, including longtime Apple fans.
Some are holding off on buying to compare other phones first, mainly because cameras matter most to them.
negative: Many commenters say foldables are old technology, so Apple is arriving late and reviewers are overpraising it as innovative.
Some feel Apple left out its best camera, such as the telephoto, to hold back a stronger upgrade for the next model.
Others complain about the high price, the shape when closed, and the display's color compromise, saying they expected more from Apple.
Many commenters say the Duo's cameras are a downgrade from the Pro models and don't justify its high price.
Some would buy it if it had the Pro's main lens or full lens setup, and could skip the telephoto.
Other complaints include a high price in some regions, a matte display, weaker battery, extra weight and missing features.

positive: Some say Face ID was a dealbreaker for them, but Apple Watch unlock support made the device appealing.
A minority disagree, arguing Face ID is better than Touch ID or that Apple's face system is unmatched.
negative: Lacking Face ID is treated as a dealbreaker by some viewers, who see it as a serious drawback.
Some find the phone too thick and heavy for a foldable, which makes it awkward to hold and use casually.
A few worry that relying on touch makes the device a fingerprint and smudge magnet.

positive: Many commenters repeat a playful line saying earlier Apple leaders did their parts and now the new hardware chief gets his turn.
Several joke that the foldable's larger screen lets them watch a recent Nolan film in the format the director intended.
Others praise the smooth fold and unfold animation, especially how the outer screen seems see-through, and say they'd keep playing with it.

text.text: EXAMPLE · iPhone Duo on YouTube: weekly readout

*Summary*
*iPhone Duo drew 215.5M views across 213 videos; audience sentiment score is +5, with Samsung comparisons and price shaping the conversation.*
213 videos from 161 creators earned 215.5M views and 4.87M engagements, a 2.26% engagement rate. 25.4% of videos outperformed their channel norm and 27.1% underperformed. Sentiment score is +5 (39.2% positive, 34.0% negative, n=7,008). Lift and sentiment diverge by format: first impressions are strong on both, while meme shorts earned views but sit at -22. The last refresh added 0 videos and 4 comments, so little has moved.

*Overview*
161 creators · 213 content · 215.5M views · 4.9M engagements · 2.26% engagement rate · 25% outperformers (27% under)

*Content performance* (content types, highest 3 | lowest 3)
• *Views*: First impressions 56.8M, Meme / reaction 49.3M, Explainer / tips 39.6M | Upgrade advice 7.1M, Keynote recap 13.9M, Comparison 15.4M
• *Engagement rate*: Durability test 3.39%, Keynote recap 2.67%, Other 2.49% | Explainer / tips 1.40%, Upgrade advice 1.93%, Comparison 2.23%
• *Sentiment score*: Upgrade advice +17, First impressions +15, Other +10 | Keynote recap -36, Meme / reaction -22, Durability test -7

*Audience insights* (top 3 topics)
• *Highest sentiment*: Positive Video Reactions +40, Nano-Texture Screen +27, Eager to Buy +22
• *Lowest sentiment*: Wanting Pro Cameras -18, Under-Display Camera -17, Waiting for Next Year -9
• *Largest*: Samsung Did It First 1,058, Eager to Buy 579, Price Complaints 478
• *Gaining*: none right now

*What changed since last refresh*
0 new videos, 4 new comments since 2026-10-05
:rotating_light: 'Left-Handed Concerns' mentions are up 2.3x as a share of comments week over week (n=89).
:rotating_light: 'Waiting for Next Year' mentions are up 1.7x as a share of comments week over week (n=51).

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Data through 2026-10-05. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are mildly positive. Mid-size audiences are the happiest.

Small channels: 32 of 90 videos with a baseline outperformed (36%), average relative lift 9.4. Net sentiment is +8 (40% positive, 32% negative), from n=2,528 product-side comments across 112 videos.

Mid channels: 11 of 50 outperformed (22%), lift 4.7. Net sentiment is +15 (44% positive, 28% negative), n=2,147 comments across 51 videos.

Large channels: only 2 of 37 outperformed (5%), lift 1.9. Net sentiment is +1 (38% positive, 36% negative), n=1,759 comments across 50 videos.

Caveat: the large-channel outperformer count is tiny, so treat that rate as rough. These are associations, not causes.
examples.sql:
WITH base AS (
  SELECT c.video_id, CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small' WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid' WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' ELSE 'unknown' END AS size_group
  FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
v AS (
  SELECT b.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline,
         SUM(p.outperformer) AS n_outperformers,
         ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
         ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
  FROM base b LEFT JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=b.video_id
  GROUP BY b.size_group
),
s AS (
  SELECT b.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
         ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pos_share,
         ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS neg_share,
         ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM base b JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=b.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor')
  GROUP BY b.size_group
)
SELECT v.size_group, v.n_videos, v.n_with_baseline, v.n_outperformers, v.outperformer_rate, v.avg_rel_lift,
       s.n_product_side, s.pos_share, s.neg_share,
       CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment ELSE NULL END AS net_sentiment
FROM v LEFT JOIN s ON s.size_group=v.size_group
ORDER BY v.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions is the most reliable format for mid-sized channels. It has the largest sample (n=19) and 42% of those videos outperformed, with an average relative lift of about 3.0.

- **Durability test:** 100% outperformed, but that is one video (n=1), so it tells us nothing yet.
- **Explainer/tips:** The average relative lift is the highest at 15.4, but only 1 of 8 videos (12.5%) outperformed. A single big hit is probably driving the average.
- **Upgrade advice:** 12.5% outperformed (n=8), with a modest lift of 1.8.
- **Comparison (n=6), meme shorts (n=5, 4 with a baseline), keynote recaps (n=2), other (n=2):** None outperformed.

Most formats have small samples, and these are associations, not proof that a format causes the result.
examples.sql: SELECT c.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(p.outperformer) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(p.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(p.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(p.lift),3) AS avg_lift FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY c.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
The two high-lift videos with the most negative reactions are:

1. "iPhone Duo's Camera Disappears #shorts" by Time Travel Visuals (explainer_tips). Net sentiment is -50 (14% positive, 64% negative, n=66). It has 20.5M views, a lift of 499.8, and a relative lift of 116.5.

2. "iPhone FOLD Hands-On | Apple COOKED!" by TechDroider (first_impressions). Net sentiment is -52 (18% positive, 70% negative, n=56). It has about 2.0M views, a lift of 86.8, and a relative lift of 20.2.

The TechDroider video is slightly more negative, while the Time Travel Visuals Short has far greater reach and lift. Both samples are moderate in size. Sentiment covers only product-side comments, and it shows association, not why the videos performed as they did.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT cm.video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, AVG(cm.sentiment='positive') AS pos, AVG(cm.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments cm WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY cm.video_id HAVING COUNT(*)>=10) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator_name, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, s.n_product_side, ROUND(s.pos,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(s.neg,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(s.pos-s.neg,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC LIMIT 2

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Samsung Did It First is the largest topic, with 1,058 comments (13.2% of all). Eager to Buy follows with 579 (7.2%), then Praise for review quality with 544 (6.8%). Samsung Did It First and Eager to Buy also lead this week, with 286 and 203 comments.

The fastest growth this week, comparing the last 7 days with the prior 7:
- Left-Handed Concerns: +585% (89 vs 13)
- Waiting for Next Year: +410% (51 vs 10)
- Wanting Pro Cameras: +273% (41 vs 11)
- Apple ad parody humor: +227% (121 vs 37)

Caveat: the first three grew from small prior-week bases (n of 10 to 13), so the percentages exaggerate the shift. Reviewer's speaking style criticism (23 vs 4) and No Face ID (15 vs 1) also rose sharply, but their growth rates weren't calculated. The data comes from a comment sample.
examples.sql: WITH sc AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.topic_id IS NOT NULL), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM sc), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN d>m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=m-7 AND d>m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM sc, mx GROUP BY topic_id), tot AS (SELECT SUM(n_total) AS t_all, SUM(n_this_week) AS t_this, SUM(n_prev_week) AS t_prev FROM agg) SELECT t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t_all,3) AS share_all, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_this_week/NULLIF(tot.t_this,0),3) AS share_this_week, ROUND(1.0*a.n_prev_week/NULLIF(tot.t_prev,0),3) AS share_prev_week, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS wow_growth, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
examples.a:
Duo sits second-best on net sentiment at +5 (39.2% positive, 34.0% negative, n=7,008 comments across 190 videos). Only iPhone 18 Pro is higher, at +12 (39.2% positive, 27.4% negative, n=3,593). Its positive share matches Duo's, but it draws fewer negative comments.

Everything else is net negative:
- Event general videos: -8 (n=1,484)
- Competitor foldable videos: -3 (n=479)
- Other: -2 (n=240)
- iPhone 18: -36 (n=169, 59.8% negative)

The iPhone 18 result rests on only 6 videos and 169 comments, so treat it as shaky. The competitor foldable and other groups are also fairly small (11 and 7 videos). These are comment samples, not all viewers.
examples.sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN 'ok' ELSE 'low n' END AS n_check FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Excitement to buy is the biggest like. "Eager to Buy" (n=535) has a net sentiment of +24 (45% positive, 21% negative). The nano-texture inner screen is the best-received feature (n=152, +32; 54% positive, 22% negative).

The sharpest criticisms are about cameras. The under-display camera (n=262) scores -18 (23% positive, 41% negative), and wishing for Pro-level cameras (n=108) scores -19 (29% positive, 48% negative). Price (n=429, -7) and folding durability doubts (n=387, -4) also lean negative. The biggest topic, "Samsung did it first" (n=627), is split at -1.

The Face ID complaint (n=35, -14) has a small sample, so treat it cautiously. Comments are only a sample of viewers, and topics may overlap.
examples.sql: SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary, COUNT(*) AS n_comments, SUM(c.sentiment='positive') AS n_positive, SUM(c.sentiment='negative') AS n_negative, SUM(c.sentiment='neutral') AS n_neutral, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='positive')/COUNT(*),3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*SUM(c.sentiment='negative')/COUNT(*),3) AS neg_share, ROUND(1.0*(SUM(c.sentiment='positive')-SUM(c.sentiment='negative'))/COUNT(*),3) AS net_sentiment FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND t.pool='product' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value') GROUP BY t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary HAVING COUNT(*)>=10 ORDER BY n_positive DESC LIMIT 40
